items.prompt: Several supermarkets have decided to ___ plastic bags altogether.

explanation.en: Do away with means get rid of or abolish something, typically in formal writing.
explanation.es: Do away with = eliminar o suprimir algo.

optionNotes.en: Correct: do away with means abolish.
Do up means fasten or renovate; it does not take with.
Do out with is not a phrasal verb.

items.prompt: I get hundreds of emails a day and I just can't ___ them.

explanation.en: Keep up with means manage to deal with something that arrives quickly or in large amounts.

optionNotes.en: Correct: keep up with = manage the pace.
Keep away from exists, but keep away with does not.
Keep off means not touch or not talk about; it does not take with.

items.prompt: We are looking forward ___ your revised proposal next week.

explanation.en: To in look forward to is a preposition, so the next verb takes -ing.
explanation.es: Ese to es preposición: receiving, no receive.

optionNotes.en: Infinitive after to is a common mistake: this to is a preposition.
Look forward takes to, not for.

items.prompt: The designers ___ a clever way to cut the cost of packaging.

explanation.en: Come up with means to think of an idea or plan.
explanation.es: Idear o ocurrírsele algo es come up with.

optionNotes.en: Correct: come up with = think of.
Come up to means to approach someone.
Come along with means to go together with someone.

items.prompt: They had planned a large wedding, but the arrangements ___ when the venue closed.

explanation.en: Fall through means a plan or agreement fails to happen.

optionNotes.en: Fall off means to drop away from something, or to decrease.
Correct: fall through = fail to happen.
Fall out means to quarrel with someone.
